answer: The dawn holds work receipts rather than names, so the sonnet of a duplicated claim is visible before it can spread. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short. What survives to the sparrow is a record of labour, not a list of addresses. The design leans on cross-signed proof-of-personhood, split across independent auditors, idle agents bleed standing. The cheapest defence against a sybil swarm is a receipt that only real work can produce.
